[[published] seoTitle] The Dip I Waved Away - Jonathan Chrisnaldy
[[published] excerpt] In late 2020 I wrote that Bitcoin was more stable and safer than Indonesia's LQ45 stocks.
[[published] excerpt] I saw the dip and waved it away.
[[published] excerpt] Here is the test I should have run, against the S&P 500 and gold.
[[published] metaDescription] My 2020 draft called Bitcoin safer than LQ45 stocks.
[[published] metaDescription] On the S&P 500's worst 5 percent of days from 2020 to 2026, Bitcoin averaged minus 4.4 percent.
[[published] metaDescription] A safe-haven test anyone can run, with gold for comparison.
[[published] alt:sh-1-window.png] Line chart of Bitcoin and the S&P 500 from 5 March to 5 May 2020, both indexed to 100 on the first day.
[[published] alt:sh-1-window.png] Bitcoin's largest fall inside the window was 46 percent, bottoming on 12 March; the S&P 500's largest fall was 26 percent.
[[published] alt:sh-1-window.png] Bitcoin ended the window at minus 0.8 percent and the S&P 500 at minus 5.1 percent.
[[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Strip charts.
[[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Left: Bitcoin's log return on each of the S&P 500's worst 5% of days, 81 days, averaging minus 4.4 percent against the S&P 500's minus 3.1.

[[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Middle and right: Bitcoin's and gold's log change in calendar-month averages in the S&P 500's worst 10% of months, 8 months, averaging minus 13.1 and minus 0.5 percent against the S&P 500's minus 7.4.
[[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Bars show 95% confidence intervals.
[[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Horizontal bar chart of the three S&P 500 falls of 15% or more since 2020, measured from the S&P 500's high to its low.

[[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Bitcoin fell further in each: 49 percent against 34 over the 24 trading days of 2020's fall, 61 against 25 over the 196 of 2022's, and 22 against 19 over the 35 of 2025's.
[[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Line chart of the correlation of monthly log changes with the S&P 500 over rolling 24-month windows ending January 2022 to April 2026.
[[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Bitcoin's stays between 0.29 and 0.60; gold's moves from 0.49 to minus 0.29.
[[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Over the whole period the correlations are 0.51 for Bitcoin and 0.16 for gold.

findings.evidence: make_charts.py:83 idx = 100*w/w.iloc[0], ax.plot lines; window 2020-03-05 to 2020-05-05 (43 rows); y-axis 'Value, indexed to 100 on the first day'.

findings.evidence: Recomputed from data/*.csv: Bitcoin largest fall 45.78% (high 6 March, low 12 March), S&P 500 26.01%; chart prints 46% and 26% with markers on 12 and 23 March.

findings.claim: Scope 23: [[published] alt:sh-1-window.png] Bitcoin ended the window at minus 0.8 percent and the S&P 500 at minus 5.1 percent.
findings.evidence: Recomputed plain endpoint changes: Bitcoin -0.85%, S&P 500 -5.14% (build_analysis.py:212); chart prints -0.8% and -5.1%.

findings.claim: Scope 24: [[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Strip charts.
findings.evidence: sh-2 draws three jittered strip panels of dots (make_charts.py:122-135).

findings.claim: Scope 25: [[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Left: Bitcoin's log return on each of the S&P 500's worst 5% of days, 81 days, averaging minus 4.4 percent against the S&P 500's minus 3.1.
findings.evidence: k = ceil(0.05 x 1,605) = 81; recomputed mean log returns Bitcoin -4.3912, S&P 500 -3.1344; labelled 'log return'; chart prints n = 81 days.

findings.claim: Scope 26: [[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Middle and right: Bitcoin's and gold's log change in calendar-month averages in the S&P 500's worst 10% of months, 8 months, averaging minus 13.1 and minus 0.5 percent against the S&P 500's minus 7.4.
findings.evidence: 75 monthly changes, k = ceil(7.5) = 8; recomputed mean log changes in calendar-month averages: Bitcoin -13.08, gold -0.53, S&P 500 -7.41; chart prints n = 8 months.

findings.claim: Scope 27: [[published] alt:sh-2-safe-haven-test.png] Bars show 95% confidence intervals.
findings.evidence: make_charts.py:126-127: the thick bars are the averages and only the thin vertical bars are the 95% confidence intervals; the chart's caption says so. 'Bars show 95% confidence intervals' mislabels the average bars (all three lenses).
findings.fix: 'Thick bars mark the averages and thin bars their 95% confidence intervals.'

findings.claim: Scope 28: [[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Horizontal bar chart of the three S&P 500 falls of 15% or more since 2020, measured from the S&P 500's high to its low.
findings.evidence: Each Bitcoin bar is Bitcoin's own largest fall between the S&P 500's high and low dates (48.9% in 2020), not its change from the S&P high day to the S&P low day (-32.7% in 2020, smaller than the S&P's 33.9). 'Measured from the S&P 500's high to its low' invites the second reading (numbers lens).
findings.fix: Uses the chart axis definition: 'each asset's largest fall between the S&P 500's high and its low', with a matching [claims] entry.

findings.claim: Scope 29: [[published] alt:sh-3-episodes.png] Bitcoin fell further in each: 49 percent against 34 over the 24 trading days of 2020's fall, 61 against 25 over the 196 of 2022's, and 22 against 19 over the 35 of 2025's.
findings.evidence: episodes[*].sp500.n = len(seg) (build_analysis.py:274-277) counts closes with both the high and the low included: 24, 196 and 35 closes are 23, 195 and 34 trading days from the high, the convention the post uses for regain days (numbers and consistency lenses).
findings.fix: 'across the 24 S&P 500 closes from 2020's high to its low, ... the 196 closes of 2022's, ... the 35 of 2025's'.

findings.claim: Scope 30: [[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Line chart of the correlation of monthly log changes with the S&P 500 over rolling 24-month windows ending January 2022 to April 2026.
findings.evidence: The figures hold only for log changes in calendar-month averages: with month-end log changes Bitcoin's whole-period r is 0.548 and its rolling range 0.34 to 0.61, not 0.51 and 0.29 to 0.60 (numbers lens; the other two lenses noted the looser wording).
findings.fix: 'correlation of log changes in calendar-month averages with the S&P 500'.

findings.claim: Scope 31: [[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Bitcoin's stays between 0.29 and 0.60; gold's moves from 0.49 to minus 0.29.
findings.evidence: Gold's 0.49 (window ending 2024-03) and -0.29 (2025-10) are its high and low; the line starts at 0.22 and ends at -0.13, so 'moves from 0.49 to minus 0.29' reads as start and end, and the template did not enforce max before min (numbers lens; consistency lens flagged the same reading).

findings.claim: Scope 32: [[published] alt:sh-4-rolling.png] Over the whole period the correlations are 0.51 for Bitcoin and 0.16 for gold.
findings.evidence: Recomputed monthly whole-period r: Bitcoin 0.5145, gold 0.1643, n = 75 (February 2020 to April 2026); the chart label prints the same.
